record.context_brief: uniqueness of Einstein metrics on S^4
record.original_question: Does the 4-sphere S^4 carry a unique Einstein metric?

evidence.quote: Question 3.4. Does \(S^4\) has a unique Einstein metric?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^4$ denote the standard topological 4-sphere. A Riemannian metric $g$ on $S^4$ is called an Einstein metric if its Ricci tensor satisfies $\mathrm{Ric}(g) = \lambda\, g$ for some constant $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$. The round metric $g_0$ of constant sectional curvature 1 is Einstein with $\lambda = 3$.

Question: Up to isometry and rescaling, is the round metric the unique Einstein metric on $S^4$? Equivalently, does every Einstein metric on $S^4$ have constant sectional curvature?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the round metric is the unique Einstein metric on $S^4$ (up to isometry and scaling) is a well-known open problem in 4-dimensional Riemannian geometry. Surveys by M. Anderson and A. Derdzinski on Einstein 4-manifolds, as well as Biquard's work on Einstein 4-manifolds and singularities, list this as an outstanding open uniqueness/rigidity question.

status_evidence.title: A Survey of Einstein Metrics on 4-Manifolds (M. Anderson)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discusses uniqueness/rigidity questions for Einstein metrics on S^4 as an open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of the Einstein metric on S^4 is highlighted among open problems.

status_evidence.title: Two open problems on S^4 with Einstein metric of positive scalar curvature
status_evidence.snippet: It is not known whether a 4-sphere with Einstein metric of positive scalar curvature is isometric to the standard S^4.
status_evidence.claim: The uniqueness of Einstein metric on S^4 remains open.

status_evidence.title: Einstein 4-manifolds and singularities (O. Biquard)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open uniqueness/rigidity questions for Einstein 4-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness of Einstein metrics on simple 4-manifolds, including S^4, remains open.
